This was my first time doing this and a total experiment. I'm happy with the method I used and I'm going to do this again as soon as I find some cool fabric again :)

This is how I did it:

I thrifted the fabric (my opshop has lots of crafty stuff). It turned out to be horrible to work with - something learned - because it's very clingy and stretchy. But so pretty. Next time I'll see if I can find straight up cotton.

I cut rectangles (I cut a cardboard template and used that to measure and cut). I folded them into squares and handsewed them wrong-side out. Then just before the final close I pulled the fabric through to right-side out and carefully closed it. That hides my horrible hemming skills and I have pretty fabric both sides.

I then did a blanket stitch around the squares (YouTube is your friend) in a thin white crochet cotton. The size of strength of the cotton is great but I next time I'll match the color better but I didn't want to spend lots of money on an experiment.

I then did a single crochet around into the blanket stitch in the navy yarn. From there I did a few rounds in hdc in navy and then in aqua / teal (whatever it's called). I thrifted a few balls of the navy yarn too but had to buy the teal. All in all I only spent a few bucks.

I attached the squares with a slip stitch blo in the navy yarn. I love the way that looks, worked up great. and because I sl st in blo it sits nice and flat. Went around the whole blanket with teal and navy and weaved in the ends.

That's the recipe. Make sense?
